summary: Rory Mackenzie worked in Buddhist and religious studies, completing doctoral research under Peter Harvey. He was a teacher at International Christian College.

Rosalind Lefeber is an Indologist who completed her doctoral dissertation at the University of Toronto under Bimal Krishna Matilal and Ronald Morton Smith, having also studied under Daniel H. H. Ingalls. She was affiliated with the University of Toronto (attested 2007).

Rosalind O'Hanlon is a scholar of Indology and history who earned her PhD from SOAS University of London (~1978–1983). She was a Fellow at Clare College, Cambridge (~1988–2006), Professor at Oxford (~2006), and became a British Academy Fellow in 2020.

Rosan Ikeda is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University from 1960 to ~1969. He served there as an assistant (1969), lecturer (1972), associate professor (1977), and professor (1983–2012), and became director of the Soto Zen Research Center in 2009.

Rosane Rocher is an Indologist and linguist who studied at the Free University of Brussels and under Ludo Rocher. She worked at the National Fund for Scientific Research (1961–1970), became a professor at the University of Pennsylvania (1970), and presided over the Ludo and Rosane Rocher Foundation (~2014).

Rosemarie Fuchs is a Buddhist and Tibetan studies scholar who studied under Katia Holmes and traditional teacher Khenpo Tsultrim Gyamtso Rinpoche. As attested in 2000, she was a member of the Marpa Translation Committee.

Rosemarie Lühr is a linguist and Indologist who earned her doctorate under Karl Hoffmann at Erlangen-Nürnberg and completed her Habilitation at Regensburg. She held professorships at Giessen (1990–1994) and Jena (1994–2013), and served as president of the Society for Indo-European Studies (2004–2016).
Rosemary Radford Ruether was a religious studies scholar who studied at the Claremont School of Theology (~1958–1965). She held an academic post at Howard University from around 1965 to 1975.

Rosina Pastore is an Indology and religious studies scholar who pursued her PhD at the University of Lausanne under Maya Burger and co-supervisor Stefania Cavaliere. She has served as an assistant and PhD candidate at Lausanne.

Ross Bolleter is a Buddhist studies figure who earned a bachelor's degree at the University of Western Australia under David Tunley and trained under Zen teachers John Tarrant and Robert Baker Aitken. He taught at the Zen Group of Western Australia until 2023.

Roy Rappaport was an anthropologist of religion who earned his doctorate from Columbia University (~1959–1966). He served on the faculty and chaired the Department of Anthropology at the University of Michigan (~1965–1997) and was president of the American Anthropological Association (~1987–1989).

Roy Tzohar works in philosophy, Indology, and Buddhist studies. After studying at Tel Aviv University, he earned his PhD at Columbia University under Gary A. Tubb (~2004–2011). He took up a post at Tel Aviv University around 2011.

Roy W. Perrett is a philosopher and Indologist who studied at the University of Canterbury (~1972–1977) and the University of Otago (~1978–1982). He held positions at Massey University (~1990–2005), the University of Hawaiʻi (~2004–2009), and the University of Melbourne (~2009–2014).

Royall Tyler is a scholar of Japanology and religion who earned degrees at Harvard and Columbia, completing his doctorate under Donald Keene. He taught at Oslo, Ohio State, and Wisconsin-Madison, headed the Japan Centre at Australian National University (1990–2000), and visited Harvard (2001–2002).
Royce Wiles is an Indologist who earned his PhD from the Australian National University by 2000 and subsequently held a post there.

Ruben L. F. Habito is a scholar of Buddhism and religion who studied at Ateneo de Manila, Sophia University, and the University of Tokyo. He taught at Sophia (~1978–1989), Ryukoku University, and Southern Methodist University (1989–), and founded the Maria Kannon Zen Center.
Rudolf Geiger studied at Friedrich-Alexander-Universität Erlangen-Nürnberg from around 1913 to 1917 and later held a post at the University of Munich from around 1937 to 1958.

Rudolf Haym was a scholar of philosophy and history who studied at Köllnisches Gymnasium, Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg, and the University of Berlin. He held a post at Halle-Wittenberg in 1868.

Rudolf Kaschewsky was a scholar of Tibetology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Buddhist studies. He studied at the University of Cologne and the University of Bonn, where he served as an academic staff member from 1974 to 2004.
Rudolf Lange was a scholar in Japanology and linguistics. He held posts at the University of Tokyo from around 1874 to 1881 and at the University of Berlin from around 1887 to 1923.
